o: He is too sleepy to eat.
There is no soup at home.
qs.why: “does not like fish, so he eats rice and eggs”에서 이유를 알 수 있어요.
저녁 식사 후 할아버지가 이야기를 해 줘요.

qs.q: What is this text mainly about?
qs.why: 일요일 저녁에 할머니 댁에서 가족이 식사하는 내용이에요.
She makes bean soup and fried fish.

patches.why: Q4: distractor 'Rice and eggs' is a second reading (text does not say who makes the rice and eggs the brother eats) and the key was the uniquely longest option; replaced distractors with clearly wrong items of similar length. Q1: key was uniquely longest; lengthened distractors.

set.text:
Boy: Excuse me. Where is the post office?
Girl: Go straight for two blocks.
Boy: Two blocks. And then?
Girl: Turn left at the bank. The post office is next to the flower shop.
Boy: Is it far?
Girl: No, it takes five minutes on foot.
Boy: Thank you very much.
Girl: You are welcome.

patches.why: 'Turn left at the bank. It is next to the flower shop.' - 'It' can be the bank or the post office, so Q2 had two readings. Text made explicit; existing Korean translation remains consistent, qs unchanged.

set.q: Read: “The shop opens at 10 a.m. and closes at 8 p.m.” When is the shop open?
set.why: 오전 10시부터 오후 8시까지 열므로 정오(낮 12시)에는 열려 있어요. 나머지 시각은 열기 전이거나 닫은 후예요.

patches.why: Identity field q changed. Without a.m./p.m. 'opens at ten, closes at eight' also reads as a night shop (10 p.m.-8 a.m.), making noon wrong and 9 a.m./6 a.m. right; made times explicit.
